001package io.jstach.rainbowgum.format;
002
003import io.jstach.rainbowgum.annotation.CaseChanging;
004import io.jstach.rainbowgum.annotation.EnumAlias;
005
006/**
007 * How the core <code>ltsv</code> encoder writes a throwable's stack trace.
008 */
009@CaseChanging
010public enum LtsvStackTrace {
011
012        /**
013         * The default. The stack trace is the <code>stacktrace</code> value, escaped like any
014         * other, so every event is one line.
015         */
016        @EnumAlias({ "default", "false" })
017        INLINE,
018        /**
019         * <code>stacktrace:</code> ends the event's line and each line of the stack trace
020         * follows on a line of its own, after a tab. This is no longer strict LTSV, but a
021         * line that starts with a tab is never an event: an empty first positional column is
022         * written as the reserved escape <code>\e</code>. A literal <code>\e</code> value is
023         * escaped as <code>\\e</code>, so the two remain distinct. Removing the leading tab
024         * from continuation lines gives back the stack trace, with an exception's message
025         * escaped like any other value so it stays on its line.
026         */
027        @EnumAlias("true")
028        LINES;
029
030        static LtsvStackTrace parse(String value) {
031                return switch (value.strip().toLowerCase(java.util.Locale.ROOT)) {
032                        case "default", "false" -> INLINE;
033                        case "true" -> LINES;
034                        default ->
035                                io.jstach.rainbowgum.LogProperty.enumValue(LtsvStackTrace.class, value, "default", "true", "false");
036                };
037        }
038
039}
